title: The quotient-normalized underlying unit of evaluated reduction
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $W$ a scheme, and $D$ a simultaneous derived reduction of extension from abelian sheaves to constant $\mathbf Z_\ell$-module sheaves [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface], using the canonical abelian structures [lem-sfb-canonical-sheaf-ext]. Fix $n\geq0$, put $G_n=\mathrm{ev}_n\circ U$ (evaluation followed by forgetting scalars), and write $q_n:\mathrm{id}\to E\circ G_n$ for the ordinary quotient unit $\eta^L_S;U(\pi_{n,S})$. There is a natural transformation $\eta_n:\mathrm{id}_{D(\mathcal A)}\to T\circ D(G_n)$ such that, for every complex $K$, $\eta_{n,QK};D(G_n)(\epsilon_K);c_{G_n,EK}=Q(q_{n,K})$, including the identity-complex comparison in the termwise map $q_{n,K}$. On a sheaf $S$, this gives $\eta_{n,S[0]};D(G_n)(\mathrm{singleCounit}_{D,S});c_{G_n,ES}=q_{n,S}[0]$. Here $c_{G_n}$ denotes the canonical exact-functor comparison with complexes or with degree-zero single objects, as appropriate. The structure DiagonalEvaluationUnit records precisely the natural transformation and these two equations. No roots system, Kummer comparison or extension class is a parameter or conclusion. The identity-on-underlying-sheaves comparison $V_n\simeq F_n\circ U$ is constructed explicitly; its inverse turns the original heterogeneous underlying-map equality into the corresponding equality after transport.

proof.text: Resolve each complex by a termwise flat K-flat complex. On that complex evaluated reduction is tensor with the positive prime-power residue ring, and the ordinary quotient map defines its underlying unit. Use the inverse derived counit on the resolution.

Comparison of resolutions commutes with the quotient map. Descend the maps to a natural transformation; naturality of the universal counit gives its complexes equation. Specializing to a single complex gives the displayed single equation.

The finite restriction and forgetting functors have identical underlying abelian sheaves and section maps. Construct their natural isomorphism by identity components; after unfolding only this comparison, its inverse transports the heterogeneous equality by identity composition.

theorem diagonal_evaluation_unit_exists (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (W : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalAb W)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (DiagonalSystems ℓ W)]
    (D : DiagonalDerivedReduction ℓ (diagonalScalarExtension ℓ W)) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (DiagonalEvaluationUnit (diagonalForget ℓ W)
      (diagonalScalarAdjunction ℓ W) D n)
